summary: Ran M3-S01 (validation, owner metadata-builder, no human gate) in .sfskills/builds/case-onboarding/. build_plan.py next listed the step, set-status claimed it running at 2026-09-12T03:11:39Z, and the owning agent's AGENT.md was executed inline (the Step 6 'any other host' path) under the artefact-path constraint. confidence_rationale: Step 9: every HIGH condition holds except one - the step was in next, all required inputs of the owning agent resolved from the plan, both envelopes validate against the envelope schema, check-outputs exited 0, and no file landed outside artefacts/M3-S01/. MEDIUM on the 'a file exists that no output declared' row: deploy-order.md is undeclared in the step's outputs[], though metadata-builder Step 5 rule 2 mandates it on every run, so it is an expected undeclared artefact rather than a surprise. The owning agent's one optional input, api_version, also resolved from none of the three Step 5 sources and was defaulted by that agent to 62.0 - the same pair of reasons the M1-S01 and M1-S02 runs recorded.

process_observations.observation: Both build_plan.py transitions exited 0 and appended runs rather than overwriting history: pending -> running at claim time and running -> built after check-outputs passed, each with the owning agent and its envelope path recorded.

Every required input of the owning agent resolved from the plan itself - build_dir and step_id from the invocation, the five answered clarifications and three assumptions from plan.json, and the upstream field, record-type, value-set, layout and custom-permission paths from M1-S01, M1-S02 and M2-S01 outputs - so nothing had to be invented or defaulted on a required row.

deploy-order.md is the fourth artefact in this build to be written by contract and left undeclared in its step's outputs[] (M1-S01 and M1-S02 did the same; M2-S01 and M2-S05 declare it), so the plan is inconsistent about a file metadata-builder writes on every run.

The step's checker acceptance_tests[0].description asserts the checker verifies that every field token and the errorDisplayField resolve; check_validation_rules.py holds no field inventory and checks neither, so the test's stated coverage is wider than its exit code - the owning agent verified those tokens against M1-S01, M1-S02 and M2-S01 by hand instead.

artefacts/M3-S02/ appeared under the same build directory during this run, written by the concurrent runner for that step; this run read and wrote nothing in it, and the two steps share no declared output path.
